title: Staff Rebate Redemption
statement:
Staff collect a daily rebate at a counter by showing their staff pass. You get the staff list and the claims in the order they arrive, and must decide each claim.

Write def solution(staff, claims). staff is a list of [staff_pass_id, team, rebate_text] (ids are unique). claims is a list of [staff_pass_id, day], where day is an integer calendar day. Return one string per claim, in order:

  1. "UNKNOWN" if the id is not in the staff list;
  2. otherwise "INVALID" if the staff member's rebate text has a minus sign or cannot be parsed;
  3. otherwise "ALREADY_CLAIMED" if this staff member already got a payout on that day;
  4. otherwise "PAID <cents>", for example "PAID 800" for SGD 8.00, and record the payout.

Rebate text, read left to right: an optional SGD prefix (capitals), then an optional $, then one or more digits, then optionally a decimal point and exactly 1 or 2 digits. Spaces are allowed at both ends and after SGD or $. So "SGD 8.00", "$10", "SGD8" and "4.5" (450 cents) are valid. Any minus sign makes it negative. Anything else (letters, commas, 3 decimals, ".50", "5.", empty) cannot be parsed.

Only paid claims count towards the once-per-day rule. Teams do not matter in this version.

examples.why: Three formats of the same idea. Amounts are returned in cents as integers.
The second claim on day 1 is refused. Day 2 is a new day.
An unknown pass, a negative rebate, then a normal payout.

constraints: a valid rebate is at most 1,000,000.00
claims are given in arrival order; days may go backwards (a late paper claim)

think.q: What decides each claim, and in which order are the rules checked?
think.a: Four outcomes, checked top to bottom: unknown id, bad rebate, already paid that day, pay. The only state that changes is "who has been paid on which day". The rebate itself is fixed per staff member.

think.q: Staff H has "SGD 8.00". Claims: H day 1, H day 1, H day 2.

think.a: For each claim, scan the staff list for the id and scan a list of past payouts. That is O(claims × staff), about a billion steps at the limits. Parsing with float(text) is the other trap: int(float("0.29") * 100) is 28.

"look up by staff pass id" → dict. "at most once per day" → a set of (id, day) pairs. Money → integer cents, never floats. Text format → a small regex with fullmatch so junk around the number is rejected.

1. Write to_cents(text): strip, drop SGD, drop $, fullmatch, reject a minus sign, build cents from the two digit groups.
  2. Build rebate = {id: cents or None}.
  3. Keep claimed = set().
  4. For each claim, apply the four rules in order; add (id, day) only when paying.

"0.29" (float rounding). "4.5" (one decimal means 50 cents). "SGD8" with no space. "0.00" (valid, pays 0). "8.999", "1,000", "" (invalid). A day that goes backwards. Two people in the same team on the same day (both paid here).

hints: Keep a dict from staff pass id to the parsed rebate, and a set of (staff_pass_id, day) pairs that have been paid.
Do not use float for money. Capture the whole and decimal digits separately with re.fullmatch(r"(-?)(\d+)(?:\.(\d{1,2}))?", s) and build integer cents; pad one decimal digit with .ljust(2, "0").
Check the rules in the stated order: unknown, then invalid, then already claimed. Record the pair only when you return PAID, so a refused claim does not use up the day.

Browser note: this page's in-browser Python (Brython) mishandles optional regex groups such as (?:\.(\d{1,2}))?. Plain string checks (partition('.'), isdecimal()) are safer here, and just as clear in an interview.
explain:
Two small pieces, kept separate so each is easy to test.

  • Parsing: "SGD 8.00" → strip SGD → "8.00" → groups ("", "8", "00") → 800. "$10.00" → 1000. "12" has no decimal group → 1200. "-5.00" has a minus → None, so every claim by that person is INVALID.
  • Deciding: a dict lookup answers "known?", the parsed value answers "valid?", and the set of (id, day) answers "already paid today?". Each is O(1).

Why cents: binary floats cannot store 0.29 exactly, so int(0.29 * 100) gives 28. A payments system that loses a cent per claim fails audit. In an interview, say this before anyone asks.
complexity: O(S + C) time for S staff and C claims (each rebate text is short); O(S + C) extra space

tests.label: example 1 (three formats)
tests.why: SGD prefix, dollar sign, bare number

tests.label: example 2 (once per day)
tests.why: the repeat on day 1 is refused, day 2 pays again

tests.label: example 3 (unknown and negative)
tests.why: unknown id first, then a negative rebate, then a normal claim

tests.label: zero rebate
tests.why: a zero amount is valid and pays 0

tests.label: float traps and formats
tests.why: 0.29 must be 29 cents, one decimal digit means tens of cents, prefixes without spaces

tests.label: unparseable texts
tests.why: three decimals, a comma, empty, words, minus after $, no whole part, dangling point

tests.label: repeats of each outcome
tests.why: invalid and unknown stay that way; only paid claims use up the day

tests.label: days out of order
tests.why: a late claim for an earlier day is still checked against that day

tests.label: same team, same day
tests.why: teams do not limit claims in this version

tests.label: largest values
tests.why: the biggest amount and day fit in an int

tests.label: prefix case, minus zero, inner spaces
tests.why: lower-case "sgd" is not the prefix; "-0.00" has a minus sign; spaces after "$" and at the end are allowed; "SGD$2" has both prefixes

govtech.source: GovTech take-home: gift / rebate redemption by staff pass id
govtech.evidence: Public GitHub repos of a GovTech take-home describe redeeming gifts by staff pass id (one per team); a 2026 variant reportedly changed it to one rebate claim per staff member per calendar day, with amounts like "SGD 8.00" or "$10.00" and negatives rejected. This is a pure-function version of that variant.
extensions: The older variant: each team may redeem only once, ever. Look up the staff member's team and keep a set of teams that have redeemed. What changes in the tests?
Read the staff list from a CSV with columns staff_pass_id,team_name,created_at. Which rows do you skip, and do you fail the whole file or report bad lines?
Claims now carry a timestamp in milliseconds and the rule is "once per calendar day in Singapore time". How do you turn a timestamp into a day key, and why must you fix the time zone?

Two counters process claims at once. With a database, how do you stop both paying the same person on the same day? (Hint: a unique constraint on (staff_pass_id, day) and treat the insert conflict as ALREADY_CLAIMED.)
Structure it as a RedemptionService with an injected store so the CLI and a REST endpoint share it, and the tests use an in-memory store.
